t: Maximum Score Using Exactly K Pairs
o: Pick k index pairs with both index sequences strictly increasing, maximizing the sum of products nums1[i]*nums2[j]. In Example 1, pairs (1,0) and (2,1) give 12+10=22. Negative values matter (Example 2 picks (-2)(-3) and 5·4), and sometimes every choice is bad (Example 3, forced to lose 7). With n, m <= 100 and k <= 100, an O(k·n·m) DP over 'number of pairs chosen, last i, last j' fits easily.
k: This is a 2D longest-path-style DP: state (pairs used, last i, last j).
Transitions either advance i, advance j, or take the pair (i,j) coming from (i-1,j-1).

a.i: dp[t][i][j] = best score using exactly t pairs with i1 < ... < it <= i and j1 < ... < jt <= j. Either pair t ends before (i,j) (inherit dp[t][i-1][j] or dp[t][i][j-1]) or it is exactly (i,j), adding nums1[i-1]*nums2[j-1] to dp[t-1][i-1][j-1]. Monotonic index constraints make these three transitions exhaustive.
s: Initialize dp[0][i][j] = 0 for all i, j.
For t = 1..k, fill dp[t] using the three transitions (guard boundaries with -infinity).
a.sp: O(n·m) — only two DP layers kept at a time.

a.n: Approach 2: Memoized recursion on (t, i, j)
a.i: Same recurrence expressed top-down: f(t, i, j) is the best score choosing t pairs from prefixes nums1[..i], nums2[..j]. Memoization avoids recomputation; it is often easier to derive in an interview.
s: Define f(t, i, j) returning -infinity when t > min(i, j).
a.t: O(k·n·m) — each state computed once with O(1) work.
a.sp: O(k·n·m) for the memo table (larger than the layered version).

w: Lead with the layered bottom-up DP; mention recursion only if it helps you derive the recurrence. Critical pitfall: 64-bit scores — products reach 10^12 and sums exceed 32-bit range. Also guard -infinity arithmetic so NEG + value does not wrap around. Edge cases: k = min(n,m) forcing near-full alignment, and all-negative arrays where the DP still finds the least-bad pairing. Follow-up: reconstruct the actual pairs, or handle k up to 1e5 with convexity tricks (SMAWK / divide-and-conquer optimization).
